profile.story: Sam runs two strength-and-conditioning studios with about 1,150 members on monthly agreements, coached by a mostly part-time team of nineteen. The membership model does what a membership model should: 88% of revenue renews on a date, retention is measured every month, and there is a general manager at each studio who runs the floor and the schedule. Where IronPath is ordinary rather than good is money and follow-through — prices have not moved since 2024 while coach wages and rent both have, 820 former members sit in the system with nobody calling them, and lead follow-up is eight hours a week of coaches typing texts between classes.

P1.note: Five sources with monthly volume, cost and quality in the platform reports (q23: referrals 44, Instagram 38, Google 31, intro promos 24, corporate 8), all tracked and reviewed monthly by source and studio.
P1.why_not_higher: Anchor 4 needs cost and quality reviewed together monthly; q30 says cost per member was calculated once, in 2024, so the cost half of that comparison is two years stale.

P2.note: Forms, DMs and walk-ins all land in the member platform (q24, walked in session); response within a couple of hours in the day and overnight leads by 6am, with an automated intro reminder and no-show follow-up shown firing.
P2.why_not_higher: Anchor 4 needs a sub-hour automated response; the first human touch is whichever coach picks it up between classes, which is the eight hours a week in q44.

P3.note: About 70% of leads get two or more touches (q24) and the no-show follow-up is automated, but everything after the first automated touch is coaches texting from personal phones.
P3.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs a defined sequence used on most leads with misses visible; a lead nobody texted does not surface anywhere, and the b2 finding is that intro attendance is exactly where the funnel leaks.

P4.note: 26% lead-to-member and 55% intro-to-member both tracked by source and studio monthly; there is an intro script and both GMs use it (observed).
P4.why_not_higher: Watching the same objection handled two different ways by the two GMs in one afternoon is the anchor: the process is loose and the loss reason — price — has no agreed answer.

P5.note: Rate card on file dated March 2024, set against two nearby competitors, with 96 founding members still on $119 legacy pricing. Q28 confirms unchanged 2+ years and pricing named as a current worry.
P5.why_not_higher: Scored 2 rather than 0 because margin by membership type is genuinely known and used (q17, Doc), which is more economics than the 0 anchor allows — but there has been no review against the wage and rent increases since.

P6.note: Named tiers throughout: eight-class pack, three-a-week, unlimited, and a hybrid premium with personal training; nutrition and PT are scripted into the intro (q29).
P6.why_not_higher: Anchor 4 needs routine upsell across the team — q29 says PT and nutrition are offered at the intro 'and rarely after', so the ladder exists and is climbed once.

P7.note: Retention cohort report measures 63% at twelve months, 94% month-over-month and 8.7-month average tenure; the dormant list is pulled monthly and reactivation runs twice a year, in January and September (q27).
P7.why_not_higher: Anchor 4 needs the inactive list reactivated on a cadence with an owner — her own answer is 'they work but nobody owns them', and at-risk members are called weekly by GMs rather than by a rule.

P8.note: Both GMs own intros, a coach runs Instagram inside her hours, and leads, conversion and member value are reviewed monthly with both GMs (q30).
P8.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs named owners across the function; marketing has no owner other than Sam, and acquisition cost has not been calculated since 2024.

P9.note: P&L confirms 62% gross margin, and the platform reports give margin by membership type and studio monthly (q17).
P9.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs that margin used in pricing decisions; it has been read monthly for two years while prices stayed at the 2024 card and coach wages rose — the report informs nothing.

P10.note: Monthly close inside 15 days with a part-time bookkeeper (q20) and q21 carries revenue, margin, profit, cash and comp targets.
P10.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs the owner reviewing a close inside 30 days with targets that operate; the operating number Sam actually manages by is a monthly spreadsheet he keeps himself, and the cash target is missed with no action attached.

S1.note: The GMs run their studios — floor, schedule, intros, member admin — and q51 confirms it holds for weeks; q50 keeps pricing, escalations, hiring, banking, technical decisions, quality sign-off and strategy with Sam.
S1.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs decision rights written for most areas; nothing is written and cancellation saves are explicitly routed back to the owner by both GMs.

S2.note: Four-week test (q51): classes, billing and member admin run for weeks; programming drifts after about two weeks and cancellation saves stop entirely. A 9-day absence this year still involved writing programming from a hotel.
S2.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs a named deputy with only a few owner-locked items; programming and saves are both core revenue functions and neither has a second person.

S3.note: The GMs sell every membership at the intro without Sam, and only about 15% of revenue traces to his personal relationships (q14).
S3.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs the team closing standard business with the owner on the largest few — here the owner is pulled into every price exception and every save, which is the highest-value conversation in a membership business.

S4.note: Three team leads, two with direct reports; the GMs own new members and attendance on the weekly board (q39) and q34 rates accountable ownership 'usually'.
S4.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs managers owning outcomes and metrics; cancellations — the number that decides this business — is nominally the owner's and a miss triggers him having the conversation himself.

S5.note: Coach handbook and class standards opened in session: current and used in onboarding (q35: 55% documented, 60% used in training).
S5.why_not_higher: Only 50% is actually followed, adherence is never checked, and quality inconsistency is still on the q36 list — anchor 3 needs the core workflows documented and current, and the save conversation and at-risk outreach have nothing written at all.

S6.note: Weekly meeting observed with four KPIs on a shared dashboard and visible targets (q39), though q40 calls the rhythm 'weekly but loose'.
S6.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs 3–7 owned KPIs with an agenda; two of four have owners, the agenda is verbal, and the unowned one is cancellations.

S7.note: Class standards are defined in the handbook, attendance is tracked by slot and coach, and q31 says a 20% jump needs only minor adjustments — there is real capacity in the off-peak slots.
S7.why_not_higher: No written capacity plan; q29 concedes there are no early-morning classes at the north studio and q36 lists quality inconsistency, so the headroom is real but unmanaged.

S8.note: Membership report: largest customer 3% — the one corporate wellness account — and top five 6%, across 1,150 members. A genuinely broad base.

S9.note: Q12 and the membership report: 88% of revenue on rolling monthly agreements retaining at 94% month over month, comfortably covering fixed costs, with membership count and churn giving a forward view the GMs read weekly.
S9.why_not_higher: Top of the scale — a meaningful contracted base that the business can forecast from.

S10.note: Member agreements, vendor agreements, licences, insurance and account ownership all written and in place (q53).
S10.why_not_higher: Q52 names four unaddressed exposures — the owner on programming and saves, the north studio lease renewal, an untested export from the platform holding every member and card record, and two GMs with no deputies. No cross-training and no continuity plan.

L1.note: The member platform covers leads, members, scheduling, billing and reporting in one system, with programming software, QuickBooks, Gusto, Slack and Drive around it (q41).
L1.why_not_higher: One significant gap: coach rostering is a spreadsheet kept in agreement with the platform scheduler by hand, which is also six GM hours a week.

L2.note: Q42 'some integrations' — the platform connects leads to members to billing cleanly, and payment data flows to QuickBooks.
L2.why_not_higher: Two double-entry points remain: the coach roster spreadsheet against the platform scheduler, and the weekly payroll reconciliation Sam does by hand between the spreadsheet, the platform and Gusto.

L3.note: Q43: definitions agreed, data accurate, member and financial data connectable, backups exist. The retention and membership reports are trusted and were pulled live without cleanup.
L3.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs reports to need only light cleanup; the operating view Sam actually manages by is a spreadsheet he rebuilds monthly, and payroll hours never match without manual correction.

L4.note: 26 h/wk inventoried (q44). Billing, reminders, no-show follow-up and the dormant pull have genuinely been automated away; lead follow-up (8h), rostering (6h) and payroll reconciliation (3h) remain.
L4.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs the major repetitive tasks reduced to a few hours per role; the largest remaining task is also the one sitting directly on the funnel leak identified in b2.

L5.note: Billing runs, class reminders, intro reminders, no-show follow-up, milestone messages and the monthly dormant pull all run reliably across member operations, marketing and finance, and were shown firing (q45).
L5.why_not_higher: Anchor 4 needs reliable automation across functions maintained; nothing in scheduling, rostering or payroll is automated and no single person is named as owner of the automations that exist.

L6.note: Q46: drafting, marketing content, member communication and scheduling — the Instagram coach uses it for captions and both GMs draft member messages with it.
L6.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs AI in one or two defined workflows with results; here it is individual use by three people and nothing in the business depends on it.

L7.note: Q47 returns three of eight — someone accountable per implementation, human-review rules clear, and the team trained. Nothing is measured, no data rules are defined, and nothing is documented before it is automated.
L7.why_not_higher: Held at 1 rather than 2 because the missing item is the consequential one in a business holding member health and payment data: there is no sensitive-data rule at all, and q48 confirms member data is already going into unapproved tools.

L8.note: Q48: shared passwords on the platform and social accounts, member data in unapproved tools, unclear account ownership — against q43 confirming backups exist. Partial hygiene with known gaps.
L8.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs access controlled and off-boarding done; with twelve part-timers coming and going and shared logins on the system that holds card details, off-boarding is the specific unfixed gap.

L9.note: Q58 'trained on the core tools, adoption uneven'; q59 confirms both GMs trained with one building her own reports, full-time coaches fine, and the two-classes-a-week part-timers using nothing beyond the schedule.
L9.why_not_higher: Anchor 4 needs the team improving it themselves; that is true of one GM and of nobody else, and the part-time majority is untrained beyond the schedule screen.

L10.note: Q49: $8–14K budget, 5 owner hours and 8 GM hours a week, high appetite because the coaches adopt anything on a phone; q55 'ready if priorities stay tight'.
L10.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs budget and time named and set aside; both are real but unprotected, and the co-owner's push for a third location is a live competing claim on the same money.

assessment.owner_objective: More profit & cash flow — then Reliable revenue growth, Reduce owner dependence
assessment.owner_belief: We fill classes and we do not keep enough of the money. Members join, they stay eight or nine months, and we spend everything we make on payroll because I keep adding class times. My honest belief is that we are underpriced and I have been too nervous to do anything about it for two years.
assessment.primary_constraint: The membership machine works and nothing collects on it: prices have not moved since March 2024 while coach wages and rent have, and the two highest-value member moments — the intro price objection and the cancellation save — have no agreed answer and route to the owner.
assessment.constraint_symptoms: A 2024 rate card with 96 members still on $119 legacy pricing; margin by membership type read monthly for two years and never acted on; the same price objection handled two different ways by two GMs in one afternoon; cancellations owned by nobody but Sam; 820 dormant members worked twice a year by a campaign nobody owns; 8.7-month average tenure against a 12-month retention target.
assessment.constraint_cost: ~$63K of contribution left on the table by two years of flat pricing on a $1.05M non-legacy membership base · ~$25K of coach and front-desk payroll on eight weekly hours of manual lead follow-up · ~156 owner hours a year on cancellation saves and payroll reconciliation nobody else does.
assessment.constraint_fix: A repriced card built from the margin-by-type report the platform already produces, one agreed answer to the price objection that both GMs and the intro script use, and a named owner for cancellations and reactivation with a rule rather than a January push.
assessment.momentum_initiative: Reprice the membership card against the wage and rent increases since March 2024, grandfathering the 96 founding members — a decision that is entirely Sam's, needs no system, and shows up in the next billing run.

opportunities.title: Reprice the membership card for the first time since 2024
opportunities.finding: The rate card on file is dated March 2024 at $179 unlimited and $139 for three-a-week, set against two nearby competitors rather than against cost — while coach wages and rent have both risen since and the P&L confirms 62% gross margin under pressure. The margin-by-membership-type report has been read monthly for two years without changing a price. This prices a move on the $1.05M non-legacy base only; the 96 founding members on $119 are held out.
opportunities.blueprint: New card built from the margin-by-type report, 30 days' notice to existing members, founding members grandfathered by name, and one scripted answer to the price objection that both GMs give the same way.
opportunities.replaces: A 2024 price set by looking at two studios down the road

opportunities.title: Work the 820 former members properly instead of twice a year
opportunities.finding: The dormant list (Doc) holds 820 former members, 310 of whom cancelled inside the last year — the freshest and most winnable segment in the business. Reactivation already runs, in January and September, and by her own answer 'they work but nobody owns them.' A returning member is worth $1,320 in the year on her own q26 figure, with no acquisition cost and existing class capacity in the off-peak slots.
opportunities.blueprint: Segment the list by cancellation reason and recency, run a monthly sequence out of the member platform against the under-filled class times, and give the front desk lead the number as her own.
opportunities.replaces: A January push and a September push that belong to nobody

opportunities.title: Automate the lead follow-up the coaches are texting by hand
opportunities.finding: Eight hours a week of lead follow-up and intro rebooking is done by coaches and the front desk on personal phones between classes (q44). The b2 split shows why it matters: 55% of people who attend an intro join, so the leak is intro attendance, not the conversation. These hours are dollarised because they come straight back onto coaching and floor time, which is what the class schedule is short of.
opportunities.blueprint: A five-touch booked-intro sequence out of the member platform with rebooking links, no-show recovery already in place extended to unbooked leads, and every message sent from the business number rather than a coach's phone.
opportunities.replaces: Coaches texting leads from their own phones between classes
